description: One-entrance fresh seed (23 Oct 2026), people placed with seed 934 by the fair placement (9f74c16), never run and never looked at before recording. No mission deadline; the recording stops at 480 s: the agent layer plus the C# retreat, room ranking and sweep fixes, and the room auction switched on; The fire has a 320 s head start (NFPA 1710 response time), so heat matters from entry. Nothing was tuned on it.

fire.note: Whole-house fire from config/fire.json, ignited 320 s before the robots enter (head_start_s).
fire.head_start_s_reason: The fire has burned for a fire department's benchmark response time before the robots enter: NFPA 1710 (2020) 4.1.2.1, turnout under 80 s plus first-engine travel 240 s, 320 s on 90 % of calls (fems.dc.gov/page/fire-response-time; firefighternation.com, Engine Company Staffing & NFPA 1710/NIST Research). It leaves out detection and call handling, so the real fire would be older. Under the NFPA 72 medium t-squared growth (config/fire.json) the fire is about 1.2 MW at entry; headless model: foyer upper gas past 60 C at entry, hallway 60 C about 54 s and living room 200 C about 130 s after entry. Owner, 23 Oct: the fire looked too mild in a 480 s run.

warm_objects.temperature_c_reason: A running fridge's condenser coils and compressor housing sit around 35 to 45 C, overlapping skin and clothed-body temperatures (about 30 to 35 C); the hardest distractor for a temperature-band test.
A hob left on: cooktop surfaces run from about 100 C to several hundred; 120 C is a low-setting, partly cooled surface, far above body temperature but below flame.
A tumble dryer's drum and front panel reach about 40 to 50 C while running; near body temperature and person-sized.
An electric water heater set to 50 to 60 C shows a jacket and pipe surface of about 40 to 55 C.

launch.reason: One entrance (owner's decision, 22 Oct 2026): both robots launch from pads at the front door, B 1.2 m behind A, as DARPA SubT teams launched from one surveyed gate. Brains get their pad in the gate frame; B's real placement carries seeded error (sigma 5 cm, 2 deg) that its own LiDAR must absorb. The brains never get house coordinates.
